label: late original phase / <DEL> step, novel input, in sequences rich in w/d/0/e/c/u/b/q/v/3
explanation: Fires almost only in the later original-phase steps (t>=3, rate rising with orig_idx) and at the <DEL> step (26% of mass); essentially never at t<3 or during the copy phase (0.3% of mass). 94% of mass is on first occurrences of the input token. Which sequences it fires on depends on prefix content: rates are high when earlier tokens (esp. first token) come from {w,d,0,e,c,u,b,q,v,3} (first_tok w 5.7x, d 4.6x), and the current input being p/r/y/1/2 or <DEL> raises the rate further. Magnitude is largest for sequences that start with w/d and at p/r/y/<DEL> inputs late in long sequences (top examples mostly start with w). The predicate covers ~82% of dev mass but has only ~11% precision; no tested condition got precision above ~0.23, so the exact content dependence looks like a distributed hidden-state direction that the token-set description only approximates.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=w (+4.95), phase=2 & out_tok=w (+4.89), orig0=d (+4.61), orig0=e (+4.08), orig0=0 (+4.05), orig0=c (+3.74). Lower it: prev3_tok=- (-7.26), phase=2 (-6.91), in_tok=e (-4.61), in_tok=w (-4.42).
